name: 4th Grade Mathematics
description: Grade 4 mathematics in ten Common Core topic units: place value, multi-digit operations, factors and patterns, fractions and decimals, measurement, geometry, and data. 49 skills, each with 30 verified questions at Remedial, Standard and Advanced levels.

source.framework: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Grade 4 (same codes as the 2017 Massachusetts Curriculum Framework, which adds 4.OA.A.3.a)
source.reference: course-outlines/grade4-math-expressions.json keeps the original 12-unit Math Expressions scope and sequence; docs/math4/CROSSWALK.md maps it to these units.

standards.4.OA.A.1: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (35 = 5 × 7 means 35 is 5 times as many as 7), and represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.
standards.4.OA.A.2: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, distinguishing multiplicative comparison from additive comparison.
standards.4.OA.A.3: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted; represent them with equations with a letter for the unknown; assess reasonableness using mental computation and estimation, including rounding.
standards.4.OA.A.3.a: (Massachusetts) Know multiplication facts and related division facts through 12 × 12.
standards.4.OA.B.4: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100; recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors; determine whether a whole number is a multiple of a given one-digit number; determine whether a whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.
standards.4.OA.C.5: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule; identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.
standards.4.NBT.A.1: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
standards.4.NBT.A.2: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form; compare two multi-digit numbers using >, =, and < symbols.
standards.4.NBT.A.3: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
standards.4.NBT.B.4: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
standards.4.NBT.B.5: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations; illustrate and explain with equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
standards.4.NBT.B.6: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value, the properties of operations, and/or the relationship between multiplication and division; illustrate and explain with equations, rectangular arrays, and/or area models.
standards.4.NF.A.1: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n × a)/(n × b) by using visual fraction models; use this principle to recognize and generate equivalent fractions.
standards.4.NF.A.2: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark fraction such as 1/2; record the results with >, =, or <.
standards.4.NF.B.3.a: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
standards.4.NF.B.3.b: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation.
standards.4.NF.B.3.c: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.
standards.4.NF.B.3.d: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators.
standards.4.NF.B.4.a: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b.
standards.4.NF.B.4.b: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this understanding to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
standards.4.NF.B.4.c: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number.
standards.4.NF.C.5: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this technique to add two fractions with respective denominators 10 and 100.
standards.4.NF.C.6: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.
standards.4.NF.C.7: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size; record the results with >, =, or <.
standards.4.MD.A.1: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units (km, m, cm; kg, g; lb, oz; l, ml; hr, min, sec); express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit; record measurement equivalents in a two-column table.
standards.4.MD.A.2: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money, including problems involving simple fractions or decimals; represent measurement quantities using diagrams such as number line diagrams.
standards.4.MD.A.3: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world and mathematical problems.
standards.4.MD.B.4: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8); solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots.
standards.4.MD.C.5.a: An angle is measured with reference to a circle with its center at the common endpoint of the rays; an angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle is called a one-degree angle.
standards.4.MD.C.5.b: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles is said to have an angle measure of n degrees.
standards.4.MD.C.6: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor; sketch angles of specified measure.
standards.4.MD.C.7: Recognize angle measure as additive; solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram in real-world and mathematical problems.
standards.4.G.A.1: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines; identify these in two-dimensional figures.
standards.4.G.A.2: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size; recognize right triangles as a category.
standards.4.G.A.3: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure as a line across the figure such that the figure can be folded along the line into matching parts; identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

units.name: Place Value and Number Sense
units.description: Place value to one million: reading, writing, comparing and rounding multi-digit whole numbers.

units.name: Multi-Digit Addition and Subtraction
units.description: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers with the standard algorithm, estimate, and solve word problems.

units.name: Multiplication Strategies and Multi-Digit Multiplication
units.description: Multiplicative comparison, multiples of ten, area models, partial products and two-digit multiplication.
skills: Estimating Products and Multiplication Word Problems

units.name: Division and Remainders
units.description: Division facts and patterns, area models and partial quotients, remainders and what they mean.
skills: Dividing with Models and Partial Quotients

units.name: Factors, Multiples, and Number Patterns
units.description: Factor pairs, multiples, prime and composite numbers, and number and shape patterns.

units.name: Fractions and Equivalent Fractions
units.description: Equivalent fractions with models and multiplication, simplest form, and comparing and ordering fractions.
skills: Comparing Fractions with Common Denominators or Numerators

units.name: Fraction Operations and Decimals
units.description: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, multiply fractions by whole numbers, and use decimals to hundredths.
skills: Adding and Subtracting Fractions with Like Denominators
Multiplying a Fraction by a Whole Number
Tenths and Hundredths as Fractions and Decimals

units.name: Measurement and Unit Conversions
units.description: Customary and metric units, conversion tables, elapsed time, money, and area and perimeter of rectangles.

units.name: Geometry, Angles, and Symmetry
units.description: Lines, rays and angles, measuring angles, adding angle measures, classifying shapes, and lines of symmetry.

units.name: Data, Line Plots, and Multi-Step Word Problems
units.description: Make and read line plots with fractions, solve problems with data, and solve multi-step word problems.
